To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the intervention arm of the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial had a 25% reduction in prostate cancer mortality compared with the usual care arm; and 2) the intervention arm had a 27% reduction in prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-detected prostate cancer compared with the usual-care arm.
the overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) in patients with clinically diagnosed PC were not different from that in patients diagnosed with PC through a screening program.

1) the overall survival in men with prostate cancer diagnosed by the intervention arm of our screening trial was not statistically different from that of men diagnosed with prostate cancer by their urologists in a clinically diagnosed cohort; and 2) there is a statistically significant survival advantage for men in the intervention arm with localized prostate cancer, and a statistically significant survival disadvantage for men in the screening arm with metastatic prostate cancer.

the development of novel and effective therapies to treat cancer, with an emphasis on prostate cancer.
the development of novel methods of screening, detection, diagnosis, and treatment of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence to suggest that screening for prostate cancer reduces mortality.
prostate cancer is a heterogeneous disease, with a variable natural history, and that the risk of progression and mortality varies with the stage and grade of the cancer.
the results of this study do not provide evidence of the effectiveness of screening for prostate cancer in reducing mortality.

we have shown that a randomized trial of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening for prostate cancer can be conducted and that screening can be effective.
we found that the overall survival for the intervention arm of the PLCO trial compared with the clinically diagnosed cohort is similar.
